text:
jai: noticing a spike in support tickets — multiple customers reporting 5xx on /v1/chat and long request timeouts. gateway shows 502/504 in a bunch of traces. anyone seeing cache errors? :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ALERT: redis.cache.errors > 5% in prod-us-east-1 (INC-2026-0912)
aly: router logs match. upstream inference runtime got upstream read timeouts, but prior to that we see cache GET timeouts and connection resets to redis. sample from router:
```
2026-09-12T14:23:11.347Z router-01 WARN upstream error: 502 Bad Gateway, err="cache lookup: redis GET timeout=2500ms, proto_err=read: connection reset by peer"
2026-09-12T14:23:12.005Z runtime-03 ERROR handleRequest: upstreamError code=502 details="cache fetch failed: EOF"
```
mira: thanks. do we know if it's a client connection storm or Redis OOM/CPU?
aly: initial signs point to connection exhaustion + high p99 latency on redis nodes. metrics: connection attempts spiking, blocked_clients > 0, p99 latency ~1.8s, error rate for GETs ~6.2%.
calvin: this aligns with a prefix/KV caching pattern — many long-running streaming requests probe cache for prefixes and block when redis laggy. can we fail-over to bypass cache for critical routes?
jai: customers pushing on this — reported failures from Prod customers A & B. they want ETA.
calvin: i'll trigger a config rollout to bypass prefix cache on router for chat/completions, that's a fast mitigation (will fallback to origin model inference).
deploy-bot: Deploy started: config/redwood-cache-bypass -> target=prod-us-east-1 by calvin at 1768005320
aly: in parallel i'm scaling redis read replicas and increasing maxclients. running quick checks:
```
# redis health check
redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 INFO | grep -E 'used_memory|blocked_clients|maxclients|instantaneous_ops_per_sec'
used_memory:1423987200
blocked_clients:12
maxclients:10000
instantaneous_ops_per_sec:7200
```
aly: also ran: `redis-cli CLIENT LIST` and saw lots of clients with short-lived tcp states, many from router pools. suspect we need connection pooling and a circuit-breaker on cache path.
deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: config/redwood-cache-bypass -> prod-us-east-1 (completed at 1768005365)
calvin: bypassed prefix cache for chat/completions. increased redis pool size on router from 500->1500 and raised redis timeout from 500ms->1500ms as intermediate measure.
mira: any customer impact after bypass?
customer_ops: AcmeCorp and BetaApps reported failures starting ~14:23. Acme says errors stopped at ~14:28, BetaApps saw intermittent failures until ~14:35. I'll send an update to both and offer timeline.
aly: after scale + bypass we see 5xx rate drop from ~4.5%->0.6% in the region and redis errors drop accordingly. still seeing elevated ops/sec but latency normalized.
jai: collecting repro steps for support ticket — saved a sample cURL to reproduce the 5xx seen by customer (hit their tenant in prod):
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi"}],"use_prefix_cache":true}'
# expected: 200, symptom: 502/504 or long timeout (>10s)
```
mira: good. can we get a short postmortem template filled?
calvin: immediate root cause hypothesis: redis prefix/KV cache clusters in prod-us-east hit connection exhaustion and high p99 latency (likely from ephemeral connection storm + insufficient pooling + eviction pressure). this caused cache GETs to time out and upstream runtime didn't have robust fallback, returning 502s.
aly: next steps (SRE): 1) scale redis clusters permanently and tune maxclients; 2) enable connection pooling + keepalive on router side; 3) implement circuit breaker for cache path (fail open to origin after N failures); 4) add alert for blocked_clients and p99 redis GET latency; 5) run load test simulating prefix-heavy traffic.
mira: engineering items: add graceful fallback in runtime so cache failures don't translate immediately to 5xx (retry policy + fail-open), add telemetry hooks to trace cache vs origin time per request, and add a 'cache bypass' feature we can toggle per-tenant.
jai: i'll update tickets and send interim customer notes.
customer_ops: i'll prepare customer-facing note with timeline and action items.
calvin: assigned follow-ups: SRE ticket SRE-998, ENG runtime ticket ENG-1742, postmortem draft assigned to mira.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0912 state=mitigated (service stabilized).
mira: thanks everyone — let's sync tomorrow on the postmortem and prod hardening. :white_check_mark:
